name: Does the toilet have to come out when replacing a bathroom floor?

mainEntity.name: Does the toilet have to come out when replacing a bathroom floor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A toilet usually needs to be removed for a clean floor installation, especially when flooring will extend beneath its footprint. Leaving it in place can create awkward cuts, visible seams, and a compromised seal. Confirm who removes and resets the toilet, supplies a new seal if needed, tests for leaks, and handles disposal or storage. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate fixture handling with flooring and other bathroom construction tasks.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually, yes, for a cleaner installation and proper coverage beneath the toilet footprint. Confirm whether removal and reset, a new seal, leak testing, and disposal are included. If the toilet flange or surrounding subfloor is damaged, that condition should be addressed before the new flooring is installed.
